title: Device Groups, Automation Levels and Security Policies with ASR Rules

header.html: 1. Manage a security operations environment (40 to 45%)

Configure and manage device groups, permissions and automation levels in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint; configure security policies for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, including attack surface reduction (ASR) rules
the official Microsoft SC-200 study guide (skills measured as of October 21, 2026) and Microsoft Learn

html:
1Device groups

Path: Settings > Endpoints > Permissions > Device groups. A tenant can have up to 2,000 device groups. A device group sets who can see the devices and how much remediation is automatic.

Wizard step What you set
General Name, remediation (automation) level, description
Devices Match rules on device name, domain, tags, OS platform; a device must match all the conditions
Preview devices Shows up to 10 matching devices
User access The Microsoft Entra user groups that can see the devices
Rule Detail
Several values for one property Combined with OR; up to 10 rows per property type
Rank Rank 1 is highest; a device that matches several groups joins only the highest-ranked one
Ungrouped devices (default) Cannot be ranked or deleted; you can change its automation level and access
No Entra group assigned The device group is visible to all users
Exam tip

. A device lands in exactly one group: the highest-ranked match. Rank 1 wins. Devices that match nothing go to Ungrouped devices.

2Automation levels

The automation level decides what automated investigation may remediate without a person.

Automation level Meaning
Full - remediate threats automatically No approval; recommended
Semi - require approval for core folders remediation Approval needed only for core (system) folders
Semi - require approval for non-temp folders remediation Approval needed for everything except temporary folders
Semi - require approval for all folders Approval needed for all folders
No automated response No automated investigation or remediation; also disables automatic attack disruption for the group

The device group wizard shows slightly different names for the same levels (for example Semi - Approval required for system folders). The meaning is the same.

Fact Detail
Default (new tenants) Full for tenants created on or after August 16, 2020 with no device groups
Default (older tenants) Semi - require approval for all folders
Pending actions Time out after 7 days and are treated as rejected
Where to approve Action center > Pending (approve or reject); History shows past actions and lets you undo some
Exam tip

. Pending approvals expire after 7 days. No automated response also stops automatic attack disruption for that group (Module 4).

3Roles and permissions

Item Fact
Turn on RBAC A Security Administrator starts it
Global Administrator Unrestricted access regardless of device groups
Security Reader Loses access after RBAC is on until assigned a role
Approve device remediation Active remediation actions (Defender for Endpoint role) or Security operations \ Security data \ Response (manage) (unified RBAC)
Create notification rules Manage security settings
Exam tip

. To let an analyst approve remediation and nothing else, give the response (manage) permission scoped to the right device groups.

4Security policies and ASR rules

Attack surface reduction (ASR) rules block risky behaviors such as Office apps starting child processes. They need Defender Antivirus as primary and active, with real-time protection and cloud-delivered protection on.

ASR mode Value
Not configured 5
Disabled (Off) 0
Block 1
Audit 2
Warn 6 (the user can click Unblock for 24 hours)

Standard protection rules, safe to block without an audit phase: block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers, block credential stealing from the LSASS process, block persistence through WMI event subscription. Warn is not supported for the LSASS rule or for the Office code-injection rule.

Commonly tested rule What it stops
Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem Dumping credentials from the LSASS process
Block all Office applications from creating child processes A document or macro launching other programs
Block executable content from email client and webmail Executables and scripts opened straight from mail
Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts Obfuscated JavaScript, VBScript or PowerShell
Block Win32 API calls from Office macros Macros that call Win32 APIs to run code
Block persistence through WMI event subscription Fileless persistence through WMI

Every rule has a GUID. PowerShell and custom policies identify a rule by its GUID in -AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Ids; you do not need to memorize the GUIDs.

5Deploying ASR rules

Method Note
Intune endpoint security, Attack surface reduction policy Recommended; assigned to device groups
Defender portal endpoint security policies Same policy type from the Defender portal
Intune custom profile (OMA-URI), other MDM Through the Policy CSP
Configuration Manager, Group Policy Group Policy path: Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Microsoft Defender Exploit Guard > Attack Surface Reduction
PowerShell Set-MpPreference overwrites the rule list; Add-MpPreference adds; Remove-MpPreference removes

PowerShell uses -AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Ids and -AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Actions (Enabled, AuditMode, Warn, Disabled, NotConfigured). Group Policy and MDM overwrite local PowerShell settings.

Exclusions Supported by
Global ASR rule exclusions All methods (-AttackSurfaceReductionOnlyExclusions in PowerShell)
Per-rule exclusions Group Policy, Intune endpoint security, Defender portal only

6Monitoring ASR rules

Place What you get
Reports > Endpoints > Attack surface reduction rules (or security.microsoft.com/asr) Tabs Detections, Configuration, Add exclusions; needs Plan 2 or Defender for Business
Advanced hunting Table DeviceEvents, filter ActionType startswith "Asr"; audit events end with Audited
Event Viewer Audit events such as ID 1122
Exam tip

. Audit first, then Block. The ASR report and DeviceEvents with ActionType starting with Asr show what a rule would have blocked.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A Windows 11 laptop has the tag Finance and matches two device groups: a group ranked 1 and a group ranked 3. Which group does the device join?

  • ABoth groups, because a device can be in many groups
  • BThe group ranked 3, because the higher number wins
  • CUngrouped devices, because the matches conflict
  • DThe group ranked 1, because the highest rank wins
Show the answer

Answer: D. A device joins only the highest-ranked group it matches, and rank 1 is highest.

S2A new tenant was created in 2025 and has no device groups. Which automation level applies by default?

  • AFull - remediate threats automatically
  • BSemi - require approval for all folders
  • CNo automated response for every device
  • DSemi - require approval for core folders
Show the answer

Answer: A. Tenants created on or after August 16, 2020 with no device groups default to full automation.

S3A remediation action waits in the Action center and nobody approves it. What happens after 7 days?

  • AThe action times out and is treated as rejected
  • BThe action runs automatically with full approval
  • CThe action stays pending until a person decides
  • DThe action moves to the history tab as completed
Show the answer

Answer: A. Pending actions time out after 7 days and are treated as rejected.

S4An administrator wants to add an ASR rule in audit mode with PowerShell without removing the rules already configured. Which cmdlet should be used?

  • ASet-MpPreference, which replaces the existing rule list
  • BAdd-MpPreference, which appends to the existing rule list
  • CRemove-MpPreference, which deletes a rule configuration
  • DGet-MpPreference, which only displays the current rules and values
Show the answer

Answer: B. Add-MpPreference adds rules; Set-MpPreference overwrites the list.

S5An analyst must see which ASR rules would have blocked activity in audit mode, in a portal report. Where should the analyst look?

  • ASettings > Endpoints > Rules > Alert suppression
  • BAssets > Identities > Identity inventory
  • CReports > Endpoints > Attack surface reduction rules
  • DSettings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Email notifications
Show the answer

Answer: C. The ASR rules report has Detections, Configuration and Add exclusions tabs.

S6A team needs an exclusion that applies to one ASR rule only, not to all rules. Which deployment methods support a per-rule exclusion?

  • AGroup Policy, Intune endpoint security or the Defender portal
  • BLocal PowerShell with Set-MpPreference on each device
  • CAny method, because all support per-rule exclusions
  • DConfiguration Manager only, through a task sequence
Show the answer

Answer: A. Per-rule exclusions are supported by Group Policy, Intune endpoint security and the Defender portal.

7.2 Recall questions

R1What is the maximum number of device groups per tenant?

Show the answer

2,000.

R2Which rank is the highest?

Show the answer

Rank 1.

R3After how long do pending actions time out?

Show the answer

7 days (treated as rejected).

R4Which ASR mode lets users unblock for 24 hours?

Show the answer

Warn.

R5Which cmdlet overwrites the ASR rule list?

Show the answer

Set-MpPreference.

R6Which hunting table holds ASR events?

Show the answer

DeviceEvents (ActionType starts with Asr).

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Device groups Settings > Endpoints > Permissions > Device groups; 2,000 max; rank 1 wins
Automation levels Full, three Semi levels, No automated response; pending actions expire in 7 days
Approve Active remediation actions or Response (manage)
ASR modes 0 off, 1 block, 2 audit, 5 not configured, 6 warn
Deploy Intune endpoint security (recommended), Group Policy, PowerShell Add or Set
Monitor ASR report, DeviceEvents ActionType Asr*
